title: Childhood games, sports and renting bicycles
summary: Baseball and tackle football on the green, hopscotch, cowboys and Indians, and shining shoes for bicycle money.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, as a child, we were talking about, like, games. When you were a kid, do you remember what games y'all played?

Oh, yeah, well, the games that we played, not the Spokin games, just the other games. Yeah. Oh, well, football. I played baseball, football. But I was never really good in basketball. But I was a pretty good baseball player. And I could run. I always could run by.
Did you play formally, like with a team?

No, we'd get out on the green. See, on the causeway there, right between, right at Andover Street, all the way back. See, we used to call that the green. They had a baseball diamond out there. And this is where all of our sporting events was. And they had a game out there. See, like this time of the OZ, they had a football game or baseball game all day. And you see, that's why I said that we came up the hard way. See, we played tackle with nothing on them. I mean, busting your head up. I used to go home every, I used to go home with all my legs bleeding, my hand bleeding. You know, from being tackled or tackling somebody.
We're pretty tough. Real tough. What other kind of games is a child, not sports?

Other than sports? Well, I remember playing hopscotch. We played hide and we played cowboys and Indians. That was a big thing, cowboys and Indians. You know, you got a dog, I got you. And hiding. And that's it. And then we got to, on Sundays, at the church, we used to go rent a bicycle. See, they had to play back on Metairie Road, where you go rent a bicycle for 10 cents an hour. And we go rent, I remember one. Yeah.
Was it tough for you to get to 10 cents?

Well, I'd find some kind of way to get it. Somebody, you know, shine shoes. Well, I kept a shoe shine box. And we go back there and run, sometimes, you know, sometimes I have enough to two hours. I'm saying 10 cents, but maybe it might have been Nicola hour. No, it had to be because they had different bicycles. They had the Nicola hour bike and they had the 10 cents hour bike. And so... When did you start shining shoes? What was the time?
